Entropion is a condition where the eyelid turns inward, causing the eyelashes and skin to rub against the eye. This can lead to significant discomfort, irritation, and potential damage to the eye. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified oculoplastic surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in entropion repair eye surgery. Serving patients in Cincinnati, Dayton, our team is dedicated to providing advanced surgical solutions to restore eyelid function and enhance your eye health.

Understanding Entropion and Its Impact

Entropion occurs when the eyelid, typically the lower eyelid, turns inward toward the eye. This inward turning can be caused by muscle weakness, scarring, inflammation, or congenital factors. If left untreated, entropion can lead to chronic eye irritation, infections, and corneal damage.

Symptoms of Entropion Eyelids

Common symptoms of entropion include:

Eye Irritation

Constant rubbing of the eyelashes and skin against the eye can cause redness and irritation.

Excessive Tearing

The eye may produce more tears in response to the irritation.

Sensitivity to Light and Wind

Increased sensitivity due to the constant irritation.

Eye Infections

Higher risk of infections from the persistent rubbing and irritation.

Pain and Discomfort

Persistent discomfort and a gritty feeling in the eye.

Corneal Damage

Potential for corneal abrasions and ulcers due to the friction.

Causes of Entropion

Entropion can result from several factors, including:

Aging

Natural aging process leading to muscle weakness and laxity in the eyelids.

Scarring

Previous surgeries, injuries, or skin conditions causing scarring and pulling of the eyelid inward.

Inflammatory Conditions

Chronic inflammation affecting the eyelid muscles and tissues.

Congenital Entropion

Present at birth due to developmental abnormalities.

Entropion Repair Eye Surgery

Entropion repair surgery aims to correct the inward turning of the eyelid, alleviating symptoms and preventing further eye damage. At AestheticEye, Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament use advanced techniques to achieve optimal results.

The Entropion Repair Procedure

The specific surgical approach for entropion repair depends on the underlying cause and severity of the condition. The procedure may involve:

Tightening the Eyelid Muscles

Repositioning and tightening the eyelid muscles to restore proper alignment.

Eyelid Realignment

Reconstructing the eyelid to its natural position using sutures or grafts.

Removing Scar Tissue

If scarring is causing the entropion, removing or releasing the scar tissue to allow the eyelid to return to its normal position.

Frequently Asked Questions | Entropion Repair Eye Surgery

What Is the Recovery Time for Entropion Repair Surgery?

Recovery from entropion repair surgery typically involves mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Most patients can return to normal activities within 10-14 days.

Can Entropion Recur After Surgery?

While entropion repair surgery is highly effective, there is a small chance of recurrence, especially if the underlying cause is not fully addressed. Regular follow-up appointments help monitor and maintain the results.

Is Entropion Repair Surgery Painful?

The procedure is performed under local or general anesthesia, so you will not feel pain during the surgery. Post-operative discomfort is usually minimal and can be managed with prescribed medications.

How Do I Know If I Need Entropion Repair Surgery?

If you experience symptoms such as chronic tearing, eye irritation, or inward turning of the eyelid, a consultation with our surgeons can determine if entropion repair surgery is right for you.

What Are the Risks Associated with Entropion Repair Surgery?

As with any surgical procedure, there are potential risks, including infection, bleeding, and complications related to anesthesia. These risks are minimized when the surgery is performed by experienced oculoplastic surgeons like Dr. Henson and Dr. Pargament at AestheticEye.

Will My Insurance Cover Entropion Repair Surgery?

Insurance coverage for entropion repair surgery varies. If the procedure is deemed medically necessary to address functional issues, it may be covered. Our team at AestheticEye can help you navigate your insurance options.
